records.source: Ἐν οἷς ἐπισυναχθεισῶν τῶν μυριάδων τοῦ ὄχλου, ὥστε καταπατεῖν ἀλλήλους, ἤρξατο λέγειν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ πρῶτον· Προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης, ἥτις ἐστὶν ὑπόκρισις, τῶν Φαρισαίων.
records.gloss: In which [time] having been gathered together the myriads of the crowd, so as to trample one another, he began to say to the disciples of him first, Take heed to yourselves of the leaven, which is hypocrisy, of the Pharisees.
pieces: Meanwhile the crowd had grown to many thousands, so packed that people were stepping on one another. Jesus began to speak, first of all to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples: "Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees. I mean their hypocrisy.

L.1: Meanwhile, when the crowd had gathered by the tens of thousands, so that they were trampling one another, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to say to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples first, "Be wary of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

R.1: By this time many thousands of people had come together. There were so many that they were stepping on each other. Jesus began to speak, first to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples. He said, "Be careful! Stay away from the yeast of the Pharisees. Their yeast is that they pretend to be good when they are not.

decisions.choice: myriads: tens of thousands, a huge number
decisions.reason: The word means ten thousand, and in the plural a crowd too large to count. It is used here to show how many had come.

decisions.choice: first: goes with "to his disciples": Jesus spoke to his disciples first, before the crowd
alternatives: goes with "be on your guard": first of all, beware
decisions.reason: The word stands between the two phrases and can go with either. In 12:13-21 and 12:54 Jesus turns to the crowd, which suits a first word to the disciples.

decisions.choice: leaven: a lump of old, fermented dough kept back to make the next batch rise
decisions.reason: A little leaven worked through the whole batch (13:21; 1 Corinthians 5:6). It pictures something small and hidden that spreads through everything.

decisions.choice: hypocrisy: playing a part, showing a face that is not one's own
decisions.reason: The word comes from the stage, where an actor spoke from behind a mask. The Pharisees showed a religious face in public that did not match what was inside (11:39-44).

decisions.choice: the Pharisees: a Jewish movement devoted to keeping the law of Moses in every part of daily life
decisions.reason: They were respected teachers among the people, and Jesus had eaten at a Pharisee's table just before this (11:37-54).

decisions.choice: yeast (B, R); leaven (L)
decisions.reason: "Leaven" is no longer an everyday word. Balanced and Readable say "yeast", which does the same work.

decisions.choice: Their yeast is that they pretend to be good when they are not.
decisions.reason: Readable explains what hypocrisy is.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs on to 12:12
decisions.reason: Jesus' words in 12:1-12 are one speech.

records.heading: The leaven of the Pharisees

records.source: οὐδὲν δὲ συγκεκαλυμμένον ἐστὶν ὃ οὐκ ἀποκαλυφθήσεται, καὶ κρυπτὸν ὃ οὐ γνωσθήσεται.
records.gloss: Nothing now covered up is which not will be revealed, and hidden which not will be known.
pieces: Everything that is covered up now will be uncovered, and every secret will come out.

L.2: And nothing is covered up that will not be uncovered, nor hidden that will not be known.

R.2: Everything people try to cover up will be uncovered. Every secret will be made known.

decisions.choice: covered up ... uncovered; hidden ... known: two matching sayings that say the same thing
decisions.reason: The two halves repeat each other, as Hebrew poetry does. Pretending cannot last, because in the end God will bring everything into the open (8:17).

decisions.choice: will be uncovered: at the judgment, by God
alternatives: found out by other people in this life
decisions.reason: The passive points to God. The verses that follow speak of God's judgment (12:4-5).

decisions.choice: Everything ... will be
alternatives: Nothing is ... that will not be
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the double negative into a plain statement with the same meaning.

records.source: ἀνθ’ ὧν ὅσα ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ εἴπατε ἐν τῷ φωτὶ ἀκουσθήσεται, καὶ ὃ πρὸς τὸ οὖς ἐλαλήσατε ἐν τοῖς ταμείοις κηρυχθήσεται ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων.
records.gloss: Instead of which whatever in the darkness you have said in the light will be heard, and what to the ear you have spoken in the inner rooms will be proclaimed upon the housetops.
pieces: So anything you said in the dark will be heard in broad daylight. Anything you spoke into someone's ear in a back room will be announced from the tops of the houses.

L.3: Therefore whatever you have said in the darkness will be heard in the light, and what you have spoken into the ear in the inner rooms will be proclaimed upon the housetops.

R.3: So what you have said in the dark will be heard in the daylight. And what you have whispered behind closed doors will be shouted from the roofs for everyone to hear.

decisions.choice: therefore: because nothing stays hidden (12:2)
alternatives: because (giving a reason for what came before)
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "because" or "so then". Here it draws out the result of 12:2.

decisions.choice: inner rooms; housetops: the most private place and the most public place
decisions.reason: The inner room was a room with no outside door or window, the place to hide or talk in secret. Roofs were flat, and from them a person could call out to the whole street.

decisions.choice: spoken into the ear: whispered
decisions.reason: To speak into someone's ear is to whisper.

decisions.choice: whispered behind closed doors
alternatives: spoken into the ear in the inner rooms
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the two pictures in everyday words.

decisions.choice: for everyone to hear
decisions.reason: Readable says why things were shouted from roofs.

records.source: Λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν τοῖς φίλοις μου, μὴ φοβηθῆτε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀποκτεινόντων τὸ σῶμα καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα μὴ ἐχόντων περισσότερόν τι ποιῆσαι.
records.gloss: I say now to you the friends of me, not you should fear because of those killing the body and after these things not having more anything to do.
pieces: My friends, I tell you this: do not be afraid of people who can kill the body but then can do nothing further.

L.4: And I say to you, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} friends, do not fear those who kill the body and after that have nothing more that they can do.

R.4: My friends, I tell you: do not be afraid of people. They can kill your body, but after that there is nothing more they can do to you.

decisions.choice: my friends: those who belong to Jesus and share his trust
decisions.reason: Only here in the first three Gospels does Jesus call his disciples his friends (compare John 15:14-15). The word comes as he warns them about danger.

decisions.choice: kill the body: people can take this life, but not the life to come
alternatives: the body as opposed to an immortal soul as a teaching about human nature
decisions.reason: The point is how far human power reaches. Killing is the worst that people can do; it is not the end of a person before God (12:5).

records.heading: The one to fear

records.source: ὑποδείξω δὲ ὑμῖν τίνα φοβηθῆτε· φοβήθητε τὸν μετὰ τὸ ἀποκτεῖναι ἔχοντα ἐξουσίαν ἐμβαλεῖν εἰς τὴν γέενναν· ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, τοῦτον φοβήθητε.
records.gloss: I will show however to you whom you should fear: Fear the [one who] after the killing has authority to cast into the Gehenna. Yes, I say to you, him fear.
pieces: I will point out the one you should fear. Fear the one who, after the killing is done, has the right to throw you into hell. Yes, I tell you, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one to fear.

L.5: But I will show you whom you should fear: fear the one who, after the killing, has authority to throw into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.5: I will tell you who you should be afraid of. Be afraid of God. After you die, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has the power to throw you into hell. Yes, I tell you, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one to be afraid of.

decisions.choice: the one who has authority to throw into Gehenna: God, the judge of all
decisions.reason: Only God has the right to judge after death. The next verses go straight on to God's care for the smallest bird (12:6-7), so the one to fear is the same God who cares. The devil is never said to have authority to throw anyone into Gehenna.

decisions.choice: Gehenna: the place of final judgment by fire
decisions.reason: Gehenna was the valley of Hinnom south of Jerusalem, where children had once been burned as sacrifices (Jeremiah 7:31-32). Its name became a name for the fire of God's final judgment (Matthew 5:22). It is not the same word as Hades, the place of the dead (10:15; 16:23).

decisions.choice: authority: the right and the power to act
decisions.reason: The word is the one used of the authority God gave Jesus and the Twelve (9:1). Here it is God's own right to judge.

decisions.choice: fear: reverent fear of God, the fear of one who will answer to him
decisions.reason: The same verb is used for fear of people (12:4) and fear of God. Fearing God is the beginning of wisdom (Proverbs 1:7), and it frees a person from the fear of people.

decisions.choice: hell (B, R); Gehenna (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the place name. Balanced and Readable use the word that names the place of final judgment, as Matthew 5:22 does.

decisions.choice: Be afraid of God.
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: throw you into hell
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the object unstated; Balanced and Readable supply "you" from the context.

records.source: οὐχὶ πέντε στρουθία πωλοῦνται ἀσσαρίων δύο;
records.gloss: Not five sparrows are sold for assaria two?
pieces: You can buy five sparrows for {{units:two pennies|two assaria}}, can you not?

L.6: Are not five sparrows sold for two assaria?

R.6: Five sparrows are sold for only {{units:two pennies|two assaria}}.

decisions.choice: sparrows: small birds sold cheaply for food
decisions.reason: Small birds were sold in the market as food for the poor. They were among the cheapest things one could buy.

decisions.choice: assarion: a small copper coin
decisions.reason: An assarion was a Roman copper coin worth a sixteenth of a denarius, the day's wage of a laborer (Matthew 20:2). Two of them bought five sparrows; in Matthew 10:29 one buys two, so a fifth bird was thrown in for the larger purchase.

decisions.choice: {{units:two pennies|two assaria}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a modern small coin by default, with the original coin as the alternative, as Matthew 5:26 does. Literal keeps the original coin.

decisions.choice: a statement (R); a statement with a question tag (B)
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer yes; Readable gives the answer, and Balanced asks for agreement in a natural way.

records.source: καὶ ἓν ἐξ αὐτῶν οὐκ ἔστιν ἐπιλελησμένον ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: And one of them not is forgotten before the God.
pieces: Yet God does not forget a single one of them.

L.6: And not one of them is forgotten before God.

R.6: But God does not forget even one of them.

decisions.choice: forgotten before God: overlooked by God
alternatives: forgotten in God's presence by others
decisions.reason: "Before God" is a reverent way of saying "by God". God keeps even the cheapest bird in mind.

decisions.choice: God does not forget
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make God the subject, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: ἀλλὰ καὶ αἱ τρίχες τῆς κεφαλῆς ὑμῶν πᾶσαι ἠρίθμηνται· μὴ φοβεῖσθε· πολλῶν στρουθίων διαφέρετε.
records.gloss: But even the hairs of the head of you all have been numbered. Not fear; than many sparrows you are more valuable.
pieces: Why, every hair on your head has been counted. So do not be afraid. You matter more than a great many sparrows.

L.7: But even the hairs of your head have all been counted. Do not fear; you are worth more than many sparrows.

R.7: God even knows how many hairs are on your head. So do not be afraid. You are worth much more to God than many sparrows.

decisions.choice: have been counted: counted by God, and the count stands
decisions.reason: The passive leaves God as the one who counts, and the perfect tense says that the count is already made. God's care reaches the smallest detail (21:18; 1 Samuel 14:45).

decisions.choice: you are worth more than many sparrows: an argument from the lesser to the greater
decisions.reason: If God does not forget a sparrow, he will not forget his own people (12:24).

decisions.choice: God even knows; worth much more to God
alternatives: have all been counted; you are worth more
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: Why,
decisions.reason: Balanced shows the surprise of "even" with a word that starts the sentence.

records.source: Λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν, πᾶς ὃς ἂν ὁμολογήσῃ ἐν ἐμοὶ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὁμολογήσει ἐν αὐτῷ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ θεοῦ·
records.gloss: I say now to you, everyone who would confess in me before the men, also the Son of Man will confess in him before the angels of the God.
pieces: I tell you, if anyone openly stands with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in front of others, the Son of Man will stand with {{gender:that person|him}} in front of God's angels.

L.8: And I tell you, everyone who acknowledges {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} before {{gender:people|men}}, the Son of Man also will acknowledge {{gender:that person|him}} before the angels of God.

R.8: I tell you, if you say in front of other people that you belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, then the Son of Man will say in front of God's angels that you belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: acknowledge: say openly that one belongs to someone
decisions.reason: The verb means to say the same thing, to agree openly. To acknowledge Jesus is to say in public that one is his. The Son of Man will do the same for that person at the judgment.

decisions.choice: acknowledge in me ... in him: acknowledge me ... him
decisions.reason: The words "in me" and "in him" follow an Aramaic way of speaking and add no separate meaning.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus speaking of himself as the one who will come as judge
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the title for himself throughout Luke (5:24; 9:22, 26). Here, as in 9:26, he will be the one who speaks for his people before God (Daniel 7:13-14).

decisions.choice: people: human beings, men and women
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}; {{gender:that person|him}}
decisions.reason: The saying is for everyone. The inclusive form is the default, with the traditional form as the alternative.

decisions.choice: say ... that you belong to me
decisions.reason: Readable says what acknowledging Jesus means and speaks to the reader directly.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀρνησάμενός με ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀπαρνηθήσεται ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: The [one] now having denied me before the men will be denied before the angels of the God.
pieces: But whoever denies knowing {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in front of others will be denied in front of God's angels.

L.9: But the one who denies {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} before {{gender:people|men}} will be denied before the angels of God.

R.9: But if you say in front of other people that you do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, then in front of God's angels it will be said that you do not belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: deny: disown, refuse to be known as someone's
decisions.reason: Peter later does this, saying three times that he does not know Jesus (22:57-61).

decisions.choice: will be denied: by the Son of Man
decisions.reason: The passive matches 12:8: the Son of Man will refuse to own that person, as 9:26 says.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: As in 12:8.

decisions.choice: say that you do not know me; it will be said that you do not belong to me
decisions.reason: Readable explains what denying Jesus means, as in 22:57.

records.source: καὶ πᾶς ὃς ἐρεῖ λόγον εἰς τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ τῷ δὲ εἰς τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα βλασφημήσαντι οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται.
records.gloss: And everyone who will speak a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; the [one] however against the Holy Spirit having blasphemed not will be forgiven.
pieces: Anyone who says something against the Son of Man will be forgiven. But anyone who speaks evil against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.

L.10: And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven {{gender:them|him}}; but the one who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.

R.10: Anyone who speaks against the Son of Man can be forgiven. But anyone who insults the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.

decisions.choice: blasphemes against the Holy Spirit: sets oneself against the Spirit's witness to Jesus and refuses God's forgiveness
decisions.reason: In Mark 3:28-30 the saying answers people who called the Spirit's work in Jesus the work of an unclean spirit. Here it stands between denying Jesus (12:9) and the Spirit's help to those on trial (12:12). Speaking against the Son of Man, as Peter later did, can be forgiven; turning against the Spirit who calls people to repent shuts out the forgiveness he offers.

decisions.choice: blaspheme: speak evil of, insult
decisions.reason: The verb means to speak in a way that dishonors someone, here God the Holy Spirit.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: The saying covers everyone; the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: speaks evil against (B); insults (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the church word "blaspheme" means.

records.source: ὅταν δὲ εἰσφέρωσιν ὑμᾶς ἐπὶ τὰς συναγωγὰς καὶ τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ἐξουσίας, μὴ μεριμνήσητε πῶς ἢ τί ἀπολογήσησθε ἢ τί εἴπητε·
records.gloss: When then they bring in you before the synagogues and the rulers and the authorities, not be anxious how or what you should reply in defense or what you should say.
pieces: People will bring you before synagogues, rulers and officials. When they do, do not worry over how to answer the charges or what words to use.

L.11: And when they bring you before the synagogues and the rulers and the authorities, do not be anxious about how or what you should answer in your defense, or what you should say.

R.11: People will take you to the synagogues and to rulers and officials to be judged. When that happens, do not worry about how to defend yourselves or about what to say.

decisions.choice: synagogues, rulers, authorities: Jewish and Gentile courts
decisions.reason: Synagogue leaders could judge and punish their members. Rulers and authorities are the officials of cities and of Rome. Acts tells of the apostles before both (Acts 4:5-7; 16:19-22; 24:10).

decisions.choice: be anxious: worry, be troubled in mind
decisions.reason: Jesus forbids fretting, not thinking. The Spirit will give the words (12:12).

decisions.choice: answer in your defense: make a defense in court
decisions.reason: The verb is the legal term for a defendant's reply to a charge (21:14).

decisions.choice: worry (B, R); be anxious (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be anxious or troubled in mind. Literal keeps "be anxious"; Balanced and Readable use the everyday word, as Matthew 6:25 does.

decisions.choice: to be judged
decisions.reason: Readable says why they are brought before these people.

records.source: τὸ γὰρ ἅγιον πνεῦμα διδάξει ὑμᾶς ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἃ δεῖ εἰπεῖν.
records.gloss: The for Holy Spirit will teach you in the same the hour what it behooves to say.
pieces: When the moment comes, the Holy Spirit will teach you what you need to say."

L.12: For the Holy Spirit will teach you in that very hour what you must say."

R.12: The Holy Spirit will show you then and there what you ought to say."

decisions.choice: the Holy Spirit will teach you: God's Spirit will give the words
alternatives: they will remember what they were taught
decisions.reason: In 21:15 Jesus says that he himself will give the words. Acts shows it happening (Acts 4:8; 6:10).

decisions.choice: must: what it is right and needed to say
decisions.reason: The verb speaks of what is necessary. The Spirit will give what fits the moment.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
decisions.reason: In 12:13 a man in the crowd interrupts.

records.source: Εἶπεν δέ τις ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, εἰπὲ τῷ ἀδελφῷ μου μερίσασθαι μετ’ ἐμοῦ τὴν κληρονομίαν.
records.gloss: Said then one from the crowd to him, Teacher, say to the brother of me to divide with me the inheritance.
pieces: Someone in the crowd said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, tell my brother to share our father's property with me."

L.13: And someone from the crowd said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me."

R.13: A man in the crowd said to Jesus, "Teacher, my father died and left us his property. Tell my brother to give me my share of it."

decisions.choice: Teacher; inheritance: a teacher of the law was asked to settle a family dispute
decisions.reason: People brought questions of property to respected teachers of the law of Moses, which had rules for inheritance (Numbers 27:1-11; Deuteronomy 21:15-17). The man wants Jesus to take his side.

decisions.choice: divide: share out, so that each has his part
decisions.reason: The brother apparently held the family land undivided and would not give a share.

decisions.choice: our father's property (B); my father died and left us his property (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the inheritance is. That the father had died is implied by an inheritance.

records.heading: A rich man and his barns

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἄνθρωπε, τίς με κατέστησεν κριτὴν ἢ μεριστὴν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς;
records.gloss: He then said to him, Man, who me appointed a judge or divider over you?
pieces: Jesus answered, "Friend, who made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} your judge, or put {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in charge of dividing your property?"

L.14: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "Man, who appointed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a judge or arbitrator over you?"

R.14: Jesus answered, "My friend, no one gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the job of judging between you or dividing your property."

decisions.choice: Man: a plain address, here keeping the man at a distance
decisions.reason: The same address is kind in 5:20. Here it begins a refusal. Jesus will not act as the man's judge.

decisions.choice: who appointed me a judge: words like those spoken to Moses
decisions.reason: An Israelite once said to Moses, "Who made you a ruler and judge over us?" (Exodus 2:14; Acts 7:27). Jesus refuses to take that place in a quarrel over property.

decisions.choice: arbitrator: one who divides an estate between heirs
decisions.reason: The word is rare and is formed from the verb "divide" in 12:13.

decisions.choice: Friend (B); My friend (R)
decisions.reason: In modern English "Man" as an address sounds rough; compare 5:20.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "no one"; Readable gives it.

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὁρᾶτε καὶ φυλάσσεσθε ἀπὸ πάσης πλεονεξίας, ὅτι οὐκ ἐν τῷ περισσεύειν τινὶ ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ ἐστιν ἐκ τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: He said then to them, Watch out and keep yourselves from all covetousness, for not in the abounding to anyone the life of him is from the [things] possessing of him.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Take care! Keep yourselves from every kind of greed. Even when someone has more than enough, life does not come from the things a person owns."

L.15: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Watch out, and guard yourselves against all greed, because even when one has abundance, one's life is not from one's possessions."

R.15: Then Jesus said to the people, "Be careful! Do not let yourselves want more and more things. Even for people who are very rich, the things they own cannot give them life."

decisions.choice: greed: the desire to have more
decisions.reason: The word is made of "more" and "have". It is the desire for more than one has, whatever one has already.

decisions.choice: life does not come from possessions, however many
alternatives: life is not measured by possessions
decisions.reason: The sentence is compressed: even when someone has plenty, that person's life does not come out of what he owns. Life is God's gift (12:20).

decisions.choice: life: life itself, being alive
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for life. The parable that follows shows that wealth cannot keep a man alive for one night.

decisions.choice: want more and more things
decisions.reason: Readable says what greed is.

decisions.choice: the people
decisions.reason: Readable says that Jesus speaks to the crowd, including the man who asked.

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ παραβολὴν πρὸς αὐτοὺς λέγων· Ἀνθρώπου τινὸς πλουσίου εὐφόρησεν ἡ χώρα.
records.gloss: He spoke then a parable to them saying, Of a man certain rich produced abundantly the land.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them a parable: "There was a rich man whose land gave a huge harvest.

L.16: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them a parable, saying, "The land of a certain rich man produced abundantly.

R.16: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them a story to teach them: "A rich man owned some farmland. One year it grew a very large crop.

decisions.choice: land: a farming estate
decisions.reason: The word can mean a country or region, and here the fields a man owns.

decisions.choice: parable: a story or comparison that teaches
decisions.reason: Jesus' parables use everyday life to show what God and his kingdom are like.

decisions.choice: a story to teach them
decisions.reason: Readable says what a parable is, as in 8:4.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs on to 12:21; the rich man's words are in single quotation marks, and the words he says to himself in 12:19 in double ones
alternatives: a new quotation for each speaker
decisions.reason: The parable is one speech of Jesus with the speakers' words inside it.

records.source: καὶ διελογίζετο ἐν ἑαυτῷ λέγων· Τί ποιήσω, ὅτι οὐκ ἔχω ποῦ συνάξω τοὺς καρπούς μου;
records.gloss: And he was reasoning within himself saying, What shall I do, for not I have where I will gather the fruits of me?
pieces: He kept turning it over in his mind: 'What am I to do? I have no place where I can store my harvest.'

L.17: And he was reasoning within himself, saying, 'What shall I do, since I do not have [a place] where I will store my crops?'

R.17: The man asked himself, 'What can I do? There is no room to keep all my crops.'

decisions.choice: was reasoning within himself: talking with himself, with no one else
decisions.reason: The rich man consults no one but himself. His words are full of "I" and "my".

decisions.choice: crops: the produce of the land
decisions.reason: The word means fruit, and so any harvest.

records.source: καὶ εἶπεν· Τοῦτο ποιήσω· καθελῶ μου τὰς ἀποθήκας καὶ μείζονας οἰκοδομήσω, καὶ συνάξω ἐκεῖ πάντα τὸν σῖτον καὶ τὰ ἀγαθά μου, καὶ ἐρῶ τῇ ψυχῇ μου· Ψυχή, ἔχεις πολλὰ ἀγαθὰ κείμενα εἰς ἔτη πολλά· ἀναπαύου, φάγε, πίε, εὐφραίνου.
records.gloss: And he said, This will I do: I will tear down of me the barns and greater will build, and will gather there all the grain and the goods of me, \v 19 and I will say to the soul of me, Soul, you have many good things laid up for years many; take rest, eat, drink, be merry.
pieces: Then he said, 'Here is my plan. I will pull down my barns and put up larger ones, and I will gather all my grain and my goods into them.
Then I will say to myself, "You have plenty of good things put away for years to come. Rest now. Eat, drink, and have a good time."'

L.18: And he said, 'This is what I will do: I will tear down my barns and build bigger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.
L.19: And I will say to my soul, "Soul, you have many good things laid up for many years. Take your rest, eat, drink, be merry."'

R.18: Then he said, 'I know! I will pull my barns down and build bigger barns. I will keep all my grain and everything else I own in them.
R.19: Then I can say to myself, "I have enough good things saved to last for many years. Now I can rest. I can eat and drink and enjoy life."'

decisions.choice: soul: the self, the man himself with all his desires
alternatives: an immortal part of a person apart from the body
decisions.reason: The word means life or self. The man talks to himself as if to another person. In 12:20 the same word is his life, which God takes back.

decisions.choice: goods: good things, possessions
decisions.reason: The word is "good things", repeated in 12:19. He thinks of them as what makes life good.

decisions.choice: eat, drink, be merry: a saying about enjoying the present
decisions.reason: Ecclesiastes uses similar words (Ecclesiastes 8:15), and Isaiah 22:13 has people say, "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die." The man forgets the second part.

decisions.choice: to myself; You have (B); I have (R)
decisions.reason: Speaking to one's soul sounds like religious language in modern English, which is not what the man means. Balanced and Readable give the sense: he talks to himself.

decisions.choice: double quotation marks inside single ones
decisions.reason: The words he will say to himself are a quotation inside his own words, which are inside Jesus' parable.

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ θεός· Ἄφρων, ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ τὴν ψυχήν σου ἀπαιτοῦσιν ἀπὸ σοῦ· ἃ δὲ ἡτοίμασας, τίνι ἔσται;
records.gloss: Said then to him the God, Fool! This the night the soul of you they demand from you; and what you prepared, to whom will it be?
pieces: But God said to him, 'You fool! This very night your life is being asked back from you. And the things you have made ready, whose will they be then?'

L.20: But God said to him, 'Fool! This night they are demanding your soul from you; and the things you have prepared, whose will they be?'

R.20: But God said to him, 'You foolish man! Tonight you will die. Your life will be taken from you. Then who will get all the things you have saved up for yourself?'

decisions.choice: fool: a person who lives as if there were no God
decisions.reason: In Scripture the fool is the one who leaves God out (Psalm 14:1). The rich man was clever with his crops but left God out of his plans.

decisions.choice: they are demanding: an indefinite "they", a way of speaking of God's action
decisions.reason: The verb is plural with no subject named. Jewish speech often spoke of God's action this way (6:38). God himself is the one speaking.

decisions.choice: demand back: ask for the return of something lent
decisions.reason: The verb is used of asking for a loan to be repaid (6:30). The man's life was never his own; it was lent to him.

decisions.choice: whose will they be: a question asked in the Psalms and Ecclesiastes
decisions.reason: Psalm 39:7 speaks of a man heaping up wealth without knowing who will gather it, and Ecclesiastes 2:18-19 asks the same about what one leaves behind.

decisions.choice: soul: life
decisions.reason: The same word as in 12:19, now meaning his life itself.

decisions.choice: your life is being asked back from you (B); Tonight you will die. Your life will be taken from you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the picture, as the meaning decisions explain.

decisions.choice: saved up for yourself
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that he had prepared it all for himself (12:21).

records.source: οὕτως ὁ θησαυρίζων ἑαυτῷ καὶ μὴ εἰς θεὸν πλουτῶν.
records.gloss: So [is] the [one] treasuring up for himself and not toward God being rich.
pieces: That is how it is for anyone who piles up wealth for {{gender:themselves|himself}} but is not rich in God's sight."

L.21: So [it is with] the one who stores up treasure for {{gender:themselves|himself}} and is not rich toward God."

R.21: This is what happens to people who gather riches for themselves but are not rich in the things that matter to God."

decisions.choice: rich toward God: rich in what God values, by using wealth as God wants
decisions.reason: Jesus goes on to explain: sell possessions and give to those in need, and so have treasure in heaven (12:33-34).

decisions.choice: so: this is how it ends for such a person
alternatives: in this way one should act
decisions.reason: The word applies the parable to everyone like the rich man.

decisions.choice: {{gender:themselves|himself}}
decisions.reason: The saying is for everyone; the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: rich in the things that matter to God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the phrase.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
decisions.reason: The narrator speaks again in 12:22.

records.source: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ· Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν, μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ψυχῇ τί φάγητε, μηδὲ τῷ σώματι τί ἐνδύσησθε.
records.gloss: He said then to the disciples of him, Because of this I say to you, not be anxious for the life what you should eat, nor for the body what you should put on.
pieces: Then Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "That is why I tell you: stop worrying about your life and what you will eat, or about your body and what you will put on it.

L.22: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Because of this I tell you, do not be anxious about [your] life, what you will eat, nor about [your] body, what you will put on.

R.22: Then Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "So I tell you, do not worry about whether you will have food to eat to stay alive. Do not worry about whether you will have clothes to wear.

decisions.choice: because of this: because life does not come from possessions (12:15-21)
decisions.reason: Jesus draws the lesson of the parable for his disciples. The rich man trusted in what he stored; the disciples, who have little, are not to fret over what they lack.

decisions.choice: be anxious: worry, be troubled in mind
decisions.reason: The verb is about anxiety, not about planning or work. The form tells them to stop worrying or not to start.

decisions.choice: life: life itself, kept going by food
decisions.reason: The word is the one translated "soul" in 12:19-20. Here it is the life that food sustains, set beside the body that clothes cover.

decisions.choice: worry (B, R); be anxious (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be anxious or troubled in mind. Literal keeps "be anxious"; Balanced and Readable use the everyday word, as Matthew 6:25 does.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs on to 12:40
decisions.reason: Jesus' words to the disciples in 12:22-40 are one speech.

records.heading: Life is more than food

records.source: ἡ γὰρ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστιν τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος.
records.gloss: The for life more is than the food and the body than the clothing.
pieces: Life is worth more than food, and the body is worth more than clothing.

L.23: For life is more than food, and the body [more] than clothing.

R.23: Your life is more important than food. Your body is more important than clothes.

decisions.choice: life is more than food: God who gave the greater gift will give the lesser
alternatives: food and clothing do not matter
decisions.reason: God gave life and the body; he can be trusted for what keeps them going. Food and clothing are needed (12:30), but they are not what life is for.

records.source: κατανοήσατε τοὺς κόρακας ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν, οἷς οὐκ ἔστιν ταμεῖον οὐδὲ ἀποθήκη, καὶ ὁ θεὸς τρέφει αὐτούς· πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμεῖς διαφέρετε τῶν πετεινῶν.
records.gloss: Consider the ravens, that not they sow nor reap, to which not is storeroom nor barn, and the God feeds them; how much more you are valuable than the birds!
pieces: Think about the ravens. They do not plant or harvest. They have no storehouse and no barn. Yet God feeds them. And you are worth far more than birds!

L.24: Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap, they have no storeroom or barn, and God feeds them. How much more valuable you are than the birds!

R.24: Look at the ravens. They do not plant seeds or gather crops. They do not have buildings to keep food in. But God feeds them. And you are worth much more than birds!

decisions.choice: ravens: large black birds that eat what they find, unclean under the law
decisions.reason: Ravens were among the birds Israel was not to eat (Leviticus 11:15). Even these birds, which no one values, God feeds.

decisions.choice: God feeds them: Psalm 147:9 and Job 38:41
decisions.reason: The psalm says that God gives food to the young ravens when they cry; Job asks who provides the raven's food.

decisions.choice: storeroom: an inner room for storing supplies
decisions.reason: It is the same word as "inner rooms" in 12:3. The rich man had barns (12:18); the ravens have nothing at all.

decisions.choice: how much more: from the lesser to the greater
decisions.reason: If God feeds birds, he will surely care for his children (12:7).

decisions.choice: buildings to keep food in
decisions.reason: Readable puts the two words into one plain phrase.

records.source: τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ προσθεῖναι πῆχυν;
records.gloss: Which now of you being anxious is able to the lifespan of him to add a cubit?
pieces: Which of you can make your life one hour longer by worrying?

L.25: And which of you by being anxious can add a cubit to {{gender:their|his}} span of life?

R.25: You cannot make your life even one hour longer by worrying about it.

decisions.choice: add a cubit to the span of life: lengthen life even a little
alternatives: add a cubit to one's height
decisions.reason: The word can mean length of life or height, and a cubit is about eighteen inches. Adding a cubit to one's height would be no small thing, so the likelier sense is a little more life, as in Matthew 6:27: worry cannot add even a moment.

decisions.choice: one hour
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the picture of a measure into one of time, as the meaning decision explains, and as Matthew 6:27 does. Literal keeps "cubit".

decisions.choice: worrying (B, R); being anxious (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be anxious or troubled in mind. Literal keeps "be anxious"; Balanced and Readable use the everyday word, as Matthew 6:25 does.

decisions.choice: {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The question is for anyone; the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "no one"; Readable gives it.

records.source: εἰ οὖν οὐδὲ ἐλάχιστον δύνασθε, τί περὶ τῶν λοιπῶν μεριμνᾶτε;
records.gloss: If then not even [the] least you are able, why about the rest are you anxious?
pieces: If you cannot manage even something so small, why worry about all the rest?

L.26: If then you are not able [to do] even the least thing, why are you anxious about the rest?

R.26: You cannot do even a little thing like that. So why should you worry about the other things you need?

decisions.choice: if then: since; the condition is true
decisions.reason: The form assumes that the condition holds: they cannot add even that little.

decisions.choice: the rest: food, clothing and the other needs of life
decisions.reason: Adding to one's life is the least thing; providing all the rest is God's work (12:30).

decisions.choice: worry (B, R); be anxious (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be anxious or troubled in mind. Literal keeps "be anxious"; Balanced and Readable use the everyday word, as Matthew 6:25 does.

decisions.choice: the other things you need
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the rest" is, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: κατανοήσατε τὰ κρίνα πῶς αὐξάνει· οὐ κοπιᾷ οὐδὲ νήθει· λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν, οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων.
records.gloss: Consider the lilies, how they grow: not they toil nor they spin; I say however to you, not even Solomon in all the glory of him was clothed as one of these.
pieces: Look at how the lilies grow. They do not work hard or spin thread. But I tell you, Solomon himself, in all his glory, never wore anything as fine as one of them.

L.27: Consider the lilies, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin. But I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.

R.27: Look at how the wild flowers grow. They do not work or make clothes for themselves. But I tell you, even King Solomon, with all his glory, was never dressed as beautifully as one of these flowers.

decisions.choice: lilies: wild flowers of the field
decisions.reason: The word is used for lilies and for bright wild flowers in general. 12:28 calls them the grass of the field.

decisions.choice: how they grow: they neither toil nor spin, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: how they neither spin nor weave
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts have "how they grow; they neither toil nor spin", as in Matthew 6:28. A few, mostly Western, have "how they neither spin nor weave". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Solomon in all his glory: the richest king of Israel
decisions.reason: Solomon's wealth and splendor were famous (1 Kings 10:4-7, 21-23). God dresses a wild flower better than the greatest king could dress himself.

decisions.choice: glory: splendor, magnificence
decisions.reason: Here the word is the splendor of a king's court and robes.

decisions.choice: wild flowers
decisions.reason: Readable uses the general word, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: King Solomon
decisions.reason: Readable says who Solomon was.

records.source: εἰ δὲ ἐν ἀγρῷ τὸν χόρτον ὄντα σήμερον καὶ αὔριον εἰς κλίβανον βαλλόμενον ὁ θεὸς οὕτως ἀμφιέζει, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς, ὀλιγόπιστοι.
records.gloss: If however in field the grass being today and tomorrow into an oven being thrown the God thus clothes, how much more you, O little-faiths!
pieces: If God dresses the wild grass this way, grass that is in the field today and fuel for the oven tomorrow, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will do far more for you. How little faith you have!

L.28: But if God so clothes the grass in the field, which is [here] today and tomorrow is thrown into an oven, how much more [will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} clothe] you, you of little faith!

R.28: God makes the grass in the fields beautiful like that. But the grass lives only a short time. It is there today, and tomorrow it is burned in an oven. So God will surely give you clothes to wear. You have so little faith!

decisions.choice: thrown into an oven: dried grass was used as fuel
decisions.reason: Wood was scarce, and dried grass and weeds fired the clay ovens used for baking.

decisions.choice: you of little faith: people who trust God too little
decisions.reason: The word is a rebuke to disciples whose trust gives way, not a judgment that they have none (Matthew 8:26; 14:31).

decisions.choice: how much more you: the verb "clothe" is understood
alternatives: how much more are you worth
decisions.reason: The sentence leaves out the verb, which carries over from the first half.

decisions.choice: [will he clothe]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the verb in brackets, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: statements instead of a condition
decisions.reason: Readable sets out the argument in short steps.

records.source: καὶ ὑμεῖς μὴ ζητεῖτε τί φάγητε καὶ τί πίητε, καὶ μὴ μετεωρίζεσθε, ταῦτα γὰρ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη τοῦ κόσμου ἐπιζητοῦσιν, ὑμῶν δὲ ὁ πατὴρ οἶδεν ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων.
records.gloss: And you not seek what you might eat and what you might drink, and not be in suspense; \v 30 these things for all the nations of the world seek after, of you now the Father knows that you have need of these.
pieces: So do not be always looking for what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not be on edge about it.
These are the things that the nations of the world chase after, but your Father knows that you need them.

L.29: And you, do not seek what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not be unsettled;
L.30: for all the nations of the world seek after these things, but your Father knows that you need them.

R.29: So do not spend your time thinking about what you will eat and drink. Do not be upset about it.
R.30: People all over the world who do not know God are always running after these things. But your Father knows that you need them.

decisions.choice: be unsettled: be anxious, tossed between hope and fear
decisions.reason: The verb first meant to be raised up in the air, and so to be unsteady or in suspense. In Greek outside the Bible it can also mean to be proud, but here, beside "seek" and "be anxious", it means to be restless with worry.

decisions.choice: the nations of the world: the peoples who do not know God
decisions.reason: "The nations" means the Gentiles, the peoples outside Israel who did not worship the God of Israel. Here the point is people who live without trusting God as Father. The world here is humankind.

decisions.choice: your Father knows: God cares for his children as a father
decisions.reason: Jesus calls God the disciples' Father (6:36; 11:2, 13). A father who knows what his children need will give it.

decisions.choice: be on edge about it (B); be upset about it (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday words for a restless, anxious state, different from the verb rendered "worry" in 12:22.

decisions.choice: People all over the world who do not know God
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the nations", as the meaning decision does.

records.source: πλὴν ζητεῖτε τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ταῦτα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.
records.gloss: But seek the kingdom of him, and these things will be added to you.
pieces: Instead, set your hearts on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom, and you will receive these things besides.

L.31: Rather, seek {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom, and these things will be added to you.

R.31: Instead, make God's kingdom the most important thing you look for. Then God will give you these other things too.

decisions.choice: his kingdom, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Several early manuscripts have "his kingdom". Many others have "the kingdom of God", which is how Matthew 6:33 begins the phrase. The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: will be added: God will give them as well
decisions.reason: The passive leaves God as the giver (12:30).

decisions.choice: seek his kingdom: make God's rule the aim of life
alternatives: look for a place called the kingdom
decisions.reason: To seek the kingdom is to want God's rule more than anything, to live under it and to pray for it to come (11:2).

decisions.choice: God's kingdom; God will give you
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as the meaning decisions explain.

records.source: Μὴ φοβοῦ, τὸ μικρὸν ποίμνιον, ὅτι εὐδόκησεν ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν δοῦναι ὑμῖν τὴν βασιλείαν.
records.gloss: Not fear, the little flock, for took delight the Father of you to give you the kingdom.
pieces: Do not be afraid, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} little flock. Your Father has gladly chosen to give you the kingdom.

L.32: Do not fear, little flock, because your Father has been glad to give you the kingdom.

R.32: My little flock, you do not need to be afraid. Your Father in heaven is happy to give you the kingdom.

decisions.choice: little flock: God's people pictured as sheep, few and weak
alternatives: a group with no special meaning
decisions.reason: The prophets speak of Israel as the flock of God, whom he shepherds (Isaiah 40:11; Ezekiel 34:11-16). The disciples are few and have no power, but they are God's flock.

decisions.choice: has been glad: has chosen with pleasure, has decided gladly
decisions.reason: The verb is used of God's good will and choice (3:22; Colossians 1:19). The kingdom is the Father's free gift, not a prize to be won.

decisions.choice: to give you the kingdom: Daniel 7:18, 27
decisions.reason: Daniel saw the kingdom given to the holy people of the Most High. Jesus promises it to his small group of followers (22:29).

decisions.choice: my little flock
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "my", since Jesus speaks to his own followers. Literal keeps the plain address.

decisions.choice: Your Father in heaven
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the Father is God (11:13).

records.source: πωλήσατε τὰ ὑπάρχοντα ὑμῶν καὶ δότε ἐλεημοσύνην· ποιήσατε ἑαυτοῖς βαλλάντια μὴ παλαιούμενα, θησαυρὸν ἀνέκλειπτον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, ὅπου κλέπτης οὐκ ἐγγίζει οὐδὲ σὴς διαφθείρει·
records.gloss: Sell the possessions of you and give alms; make for yourselves purses not growing old, a treasure unfailing in the heavens, where thief not draws near nor moth destroys.
pieces: Sell what you own and give the money to people in need. Get yourselves money bags that never wear out, a treasure in heaven that will never run out. No thief can get near it there, and no moth can spoil it.

L.33: Sell your possessions and give alms. Make for yourselves purses that do not grow old, an unfailing treasure in the heavens, where no thief comes near and no moth destroys.

R.33: Sell the things you own and give the money to poor people. Then you will have a treasure in heaven that will last forever. It will be like a purse that never wears out. No thief can steal it, and no moth can eat it.

decisions.choice: alms: gifts to the poor
decisions.reason: Giving to the poor was a duty of the law (Deuteronomy 15:7-11) and a mark of true devotion (11:41; Acts 10:2).

decisions.choice: treasure in the heavens: what God keeps for those who give
decisions.reason: What is given away for God is kept by God. Jesus says the same to the rich ruler (18:22).

decisions.choice: purses; moth: a money bag wears out, and moths eat stored cloth
decisions.reason: Wealth was often kept as fine clothing, which moths could ruin, and money was carried in a leather bag. Treasure with God is safe from both.

decisions.choice: heavens: heaven, where God is
decisions.reason: The plural follows a Hebrew way of speaking and means heaven.

decisions.choice: give the money to people in need (B); give the money to poor people (R)
decisions.reason: "Alms" is an old word. Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: the treasure first, then the purse as a picture
decisions.reason: Readable puts the plain statement first and the picture after it.

records.source: ὅπου γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θησαυρὸς ὑμῶν, ἐκεῖ καὶ ἡ καρδία ὑμῶν ἔσται.
records.gloss: Where for is the treasure of you, there also the heart of you will be.
pieces: Your heart will be wherever your treasure is.

L.34: For where your treasure is, there your heart also will be.

R.34: Your heart will always be with the things you treasure most.

decisions.choice: heart: the center of a person, where desire, thought and will are
decisions.reason: In Scripture the heart is the inner self that decides and loves. What a person treasures draws the whole self after it.

decisions.choice: for: the reason for 12:33
decisions.reason: Treasure in heaven matters because the heart goes where the treasure is.

decisions.choice: the heart first
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the main point first, in plain order.

records.source: Ἔστωσαν ὑμῶν αἱ ὀσφύες περιεζωσμέναι καὶ οἱ λύχνοι καιόμενοι, καὶ ὑμεῖς ὅμοιοι ἀνθρώποις προσδεχομένοις τὸν κύριον ἑαυτῶν πότε ἀναλύσῃ ἐκ τῶν γάμων, ἵνα ἐλθόντος καὶ κρούσαντος εὐθέως ἀνοίξωσιν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: Let be of you the waists girded and the lamps burning, \v 36 and you like to men waiting for the master of themselves, when he might return from the wedding feasts, that having come and having knocked immediately they might open to him.
pieces: Stay ready for work, with your belt tied and your lamp lit.
Be like {{gender:people|men}} who are waiting for their master to come home from a wedding feast, ready to open the door the moment he arrives and knocks.

L.35: Let your waists be girded and your lamps burning,
L.36: and be like {{gender:people|men}} waiting for their master, when he returns from the wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks they may open to him at once.

R.35: Be ready to work. Tuck your robe into your belt and keep a lamp lit.
R.36: Be like a household of servants waiting up for their master on the night he comes back from a wedding party. They want to be ready to open the door as soon as he knocks.

decisions.choice: let your waists be girded: be dressed and ready for action
decisions.reason: People wore long robes. To work, travel or run, they pulled the robe up and tucked it into a belt (Exodus 12:11; 1 Kings 18:46).

decisions.choice: wedding feast: a celebration that could last late into the night, or for days
decisions.reason: No one could know when a guest would come home from such a feast. The slaves must stay ready all night.

decisions.choice: people: here the slaves of the household (12:37)
decisions.reason: The word means human beings; 12:37 shows they are the master's slaves.

decisions.choice: master: the owner of the household
alternatives: Lord as a title of Jesus
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for "Lord". In the parable it is a slave owner; Peter's question in 12:41 and the saying in 12:40 show that Jesus is speaking of his own return.

decisions.choice: Stay ready for work, with your belt tied (B); Tuck your robe into your belt (R)
decisions.reason: "Gird" is an old word. Balanced and Readable describe what it meant.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The picture is of a whole household of slaves, and the saying is for every disciple; the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: a household of servants
decisions.reason: Readable names the people as the household's servants from the start, as 12:37 calls them. The Greek here says only "men".

records.heading: Servants waiting for their master

records.source: μακάριοι οἱ δοῦλοι ἐκεῖνοι, οὓς ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος εὑρήσει γρηγοροῦντας· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι περιζώσεται καὶ ἀνακλινεῖ αὐτοὺς καὶ παρελθὼν διακονήσει αὐτοῖς.
records.gloss: Blessed the slaves those, whom having come the master will find watching; truly I say to you that he will gird himself and will make recline them and having come up will serve them.
pieces: Blessed are those servants whom the master finds awake and watching when he comes. Truly I tell you, he will tie on an apron, seat them at the table, and come and wait on them himself.

L.37: Blessed [are] those slaves whom the master will find awake when he comes. Truly I tell you that he will gird himself and have them recline [at table], and he will come and serve them.

R.37: How blessed those servants will be if their master finds them awake and ready when he comes! I tell you the truth, the master will put on work clothes himself. He will have the servants sit down to eat, and he will bring them their food.

decisions.choice: slaves: people owned by their master
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for a slave. A slave belonged to the master and lived at his command.

decisions.choice: blessed: fortunate, in a happy state because of God's favor
decisions.reason: The word is the one of the beatitudes (6:20).

decisions.choice: he will gird himself and serve them: the master takes a slave's place
alternatives: he will reward them with money
decisions.reason: Normally slaves served their master at table (17:7-8). Here the master puts on work clothes and serves them. Jesus says he is among his disciples as one who serves (22:27), and in John 13:4-5 he ties a towel around himself and washes their feet.

decisions.choice: recline: lie on couches at a meal
decisions.reason: At a feast guests lay on their side on couches around a low table.

decisions.choice: watching: awake, alert
decisions.reason: The verb means to stay awake and on guard.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: Luke's usual rendering of Jesus' "amen" (4:24).

decisions.choice: How blessed those servants will be
decisions.reason: Readable makes the declaration an exclamation, as in 6:20.

decisions.choice: tie on an apron
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of dressing for work at table.

decisions.choice: seat them at the table (B); have the servants sit down to eat (R)
decisions.reason: Modern readers sit at meals; the meaning decision explains the custom.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: κἂν ἐν τῇ δευτέρᾳ κἂν ἐν τῇ τρίτῃ φυλακῇ ἔλθῃ καὶ εὕρῃ οὕτως, μακάριοί εἰσιν ἐκεῖνοι.
records.gloss: And if in the second and if in the third watch he comes and finds thus, blessed are those.
pieces: He may come in the middle of the night or even later, but if he finds them ready, those servants are blessed.

L.38: And if he comes in the second watch, or in the third, and finds [them] so, blessed are those [slaves].

R.38: He may come late at night or in the early hours before dawn. But if he finds them ready, how blessed those servants will be!

decisions.choice: the second and third watch: late in the night, after midnight
decisions.reason: The night was divided into watches, three in Jewish reckoning and four in Roman. Either way, the second and third watches are the dead of night, when it is hardest to stay awake.

decisions.choice: so: awake and ready, as in 12:37
decisions.reason: The word points back to the slaves who watch.

decisions.choice: in the middle of the night or even later (B); late at night or in the early hours before dawn (R)
alternatives: in the second or third watch
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the time in modern terms, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: those servants
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who is meant.

records.source: Τοῦτο δὲ γινώσκετε ὅτι εἰ ᾔδει ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης ποίᾳ ὥρᾳ ὁ κλέπτης ἔρχεται, οὐκ ἂν ἀφῆκεν διορυχθῆναι τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: This however know, that if had known the master of the house in what hour the thief is coming, not he would have allowed to be broken into the house of him.
pieces: You can be sure of this: if the owner of a house knew the hour when the thief was on his way, he would not let anyone dig through the walls of his house.

L.39: But know this: if the master of the house had known in what hour the thief was coming, he would not have allowed his house to be broken into.

R.39: You know that if the owner of a house knew what time a thief was coming, he would not let the thief break into his house.

decisions.choice: he would not have let, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: he would have stayed awake and would not have let
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts have the shorter text. Many others add "he would have stayed awake", which matches Matthew 24:43. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: be broken into: dug through
decisions.reason: The verb means to dig through. Many houses had walls of mud brick, and a thief could dig a hole through them.

decisions.choice: know: a command, "know this"
decisions.reason: The form can be a command or a statement. Either way Jesus appeals to what everyone knows.

decisions.choice: the thief: the unexpected hour of the Son of Man's coming
alternatives: the Son of Man is like a thief in character
decisions.reason: The comparison is about timing only (12:40; 1 Thessalonians 5:2).

decisions.choice: dig through the walls
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the verb, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: καὶ ὑμεῖς γίνεσθε ἕτοιμοι, ὅτι ᾗ ὥρᾳ οὐ δοκεῖτε ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεται.
records.gloss: Also you be ready, for in the hour not you expect the Son of Man comes.
pieces: Be ready yourselves, then. The Son of Man is coming at an hour when you do not think {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will."

L.40: You also be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect."

R.40: So stay ready all the time. You do not know when the Son of Man will come. It will be when you are not expecting {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

decisions.choice: the Son of Man is coming: Jesus' return in glory
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of his coming as judge (9:26; 12:8; 21:27).

decisions.choice: be ready: a continuing state
alternatives: get ready at the last minute
decisions.reason: The command is to be and stay ready, since the hour is not known.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
decisions.reason: Peter interrupts in 12:41.

records.source: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Πέτρος· Κύριε, πρὸς ἡμᾶς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην λέγεις ἢ καὶ πρὸς πάντας;
records.gloss: Said then the Peter, Lord, to us the parable this are you speaking or also to all?
pieces: Peter asked, "Lord, is this parable meant for us, or are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} telling it to everyone?"

L.41: And Peter said, "Lord, are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} telling this parable to us, or also to everyone?"

R.41: Peter said, "Lord, are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} telling this story just for us, or for all the people?"

decisions.choice: everyone: the whole crowd, not only the Twelve
decisions.reason: Peter asks whether the call to be ready is for the leaders Jesus has chosen or for all who listen (12:1, 12:22).

decisions.choice: this parable: the parable of the watchful slaves and the thief (12:35-40)
alternatives: the parable of the rich man
decisions.reason: Peter's question follows straight on from 12:35-40.

decisions.choice: story
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word, as in 12:16.

records.source: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ κύριος· Τίς ἄρα ἐστὶν ὁ πιστὸς οἰκονόμος, ὁ φρόνιμος, ὃν καταστήσει ὁ κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς θεραπείας αὐτοῦ τοῦ διδόναι ἐν καιρῷ τὸ σιτομέτριον;
records.gloss: And said the Lord, Who then is the faithful manager, the wise, whom will set the master over the household staff of him to give in season the ration of grain?
pieces: The Lord answered, "Who, then, is the manager who can be trusted and who acts wisely? His master will put him in charge of the other workers in the household, to give them their share of food when it is due.

L.42: And the Lord said, "Who then is the faithful [and] wise manager, whom the master will set over his household staff, to give [them their] ration of grain in its season?

R.42: The Lord Jesus answered, "Think of a manager who is faithful and wise. His master puts him in charge of all the other servants in the house. His job is to give them their food at the right time.

decisions.choice: the Lord: Luke the narrator calls Jesus by his title, beside the master in the parable
decisions.reason: Luke uses the title for Jesus in the story (7:13; 10:1). The same word is used for the master in the parable, which hints at who the master is.

decisions.choice: manager: a steward, often a trusted slave, who ran the household for the owner
decisions.reason: The manager here is himself a slave (12:43). Leaders among Jesus' followers are pictured as such managers (1 Corinthians 4:1-2).

decisions.choice: who then: the question answers Peter by turning it back on him
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say directly whom the parable is for. He describes the faithful manager and lets Peter see himself in the picture.

decisions.choice: household staff: the servants of a household
decisions.reason: The word means service, and so the body of servants who did it.

decisions.choice: ration of food: a measured allowance of grain
decisions.reason: Slaves received a fixed amount of grain at set times.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable adds the name so that the title is not confused with the master in the parable.

decisions.choice: two sentences instead of one question
alternatives: Who then is the faithful and wise manager whom ...?
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the long question to keep it clear.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs on to 12:53
decisions.reason: Jesus' answer to Peter runs to 12:53 with no break.

records.source: μακάριος ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος, ὃν ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ εὑρήσει ποιοῦντα οὕτως·
records.gloss: Blessed the slave that, whom having come the master of him will find doing thus.
pieces: Blessed is that servant if his master finds him doing just that when he comes home.

L.43: Blessed [is] that slave whom his master will find doing so when he comes.

R.43: How blessed that servant will be if his master comes home and finds him doing his job!

decisions.choice: slave: the manager is himself a slave
decisions.reason: The trusted manager of 12:42 belongs to his master like the others.

decisions.choice: How blessed that servant will be
decisions.reason: As in 12:37.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: ἀληθῶς λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ὑπάρχουσιν αὐτοῦ καταστήσει αὐτόν.
records.gloss: Truthfully I say to you that over all the possessions of him he will set him.
pieces: I tell you truly, he will put him in charge of everything he owns.

L.44: In truth I tell you that he will set him over all his possessions.

R.44: I tell you the truth, the master will put that servant in charge of everything he owns.

decisions.choice: truly: in truth
decisions.reason: Luke has the ordinary word for "truly" here, not the Hebrew word amen (9:27).

decisions.choice: in charge of all his possessions: faithful service is rewarded with greater trust
decisions.reason: The reward for faithful work is more work of the same kind (19:17).

decisions.choice: the master; that servant
decisions.reason: Readable names the two people to keep them apart.

records.source: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπῃ ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ· Χρονίζει ὁ κύριός μου ἔρχεσθαι, καὶ ἄρξηται τύπτειν τοὺς παῖδας καὶ τὰς παιδίσκας, ἐσθίειν τε καὶ πίνειν καὶ μεθύσκεσθαι, ἥξει ὁ κύριος τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ᾗ οὐ προσδοκᾷ καὶ ἐν ὥρᾳ ᾗ οὐ γινώσκει, καὶ διχοτομήσει αὐτὸν καὶ τὸ μέρος αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀπίστων θήσει.
records.gloss: If however should say the slave that in the heart of him, Delays the master of me to come, and should begin to beat the menservants and the maidservants, to eat and also to drink and to get drunk, \v 46 will come the master of the slave that in a day in which not he expects and in an hour which not he knows, and will cut in two him, and the portion of him with the unfaithful will appoint.
pieces: But that servant may think, 'My master will be a long while yet.' He may start beating the menservants and the serving girls, and eating and drinking until he is drunk.
Then his master will arrive on a day the servant does not expect, at an hour he has not guessed. He will cut him to pieces and put him with the unfaithful.

L.45: But if that slave says in his heart, 'My master is delaying [his] coming,' and begins to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk,
L.46: the master of that slave will come on a day when he does not expect [him] and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in two and assign his place with the unfaithful.

R.45: But suppose that servant thinks, 'My master will not come back for a long time.' So he starts hitting the other servants, men and women alike. He eats and drinks and gets drunk.
R.46: Then one day the master will come back when the servant does not expect him, at a time the servant does not know. The master will punish him very severely. He will send him away to be with those who were not faithful.

decisions.choice: says in his heart: thinks to himself
decisions.reason: In Scripture the heart is where a person thinks and decides (Psalm 14:1).

decisions.choice: menservants and maidservants: the male and female servants of the household
decisions.reason: The first word can mean a boy or a servant, and the second a girl or a female slave (22:56). Here they are the household staff the manager was to feed.

decisions.choice: cut him in two: punish him with the utmost severity
alternatives: cut him off from the household
decisions.reason: The verb means to cut in two, a punishment known in the ancient world (compare 1 Samuel 15:33). Some take it as a strong picture for being cut off. Either way the punishment is final, and the rest of the verse speaks of his place with the unfaithful.

decisions.choice: the unfaithful: those who did not keep faith with their master
decisions.reason: The word can mean unbelieving or untrustworthy. Set against the "faithful" manager of 12:42, it means those who proved unfaithful.

decisions.choice: my master is delaying: the danger of thinking the Lord's coming is far off
alternatives: a statement that he will not come
decisions.reason: The slave does not deny that his master will return, only that it will be soon. Jesus warns his followers against that attitude (12:40).

decisions.choice: the menservants and the serving girls (B); the other servants, men and women alike (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the two words in plain language.

decisions.choice: punish him very severely
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense without the picture, which the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: send him away to be with
decisions.reason: Readable says what the place with the unfaithful means: he is shut out of the household.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave". The other servants he beats are the household staff of meaning decision m2.

records.source: ἐκεῖνος δὲ ὁ δοῦλος ὁ γνοὺς τὸ θέλημα τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ καὶ μὴ ἑτοιμάσας ἢ ποιήσας πρὸς τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ δαρήσεται πολλάς·
records.gloss: That now the slave, the [one] having known the will of the master of him and not having prepared or having done according to the will of him, will be beaten with many [blows];
pieces: A servant who knew his master's wishes but made no preparations and did not carry them out will receive a heavy beating.

L.47: And that slave who knew his master's will and did not prepare or act according to it will be beaten with many [blows];

R.47: Suppose a servant knows what his master wants him to do, but he does not prepare and does not do it. He will be whipped many times.

decisions.choice: beaten with many blows: flogged
decisions.reason: Masters beat slaves as punishment. The picture is of God's judgment, which takes account of what each person knew.

decisions.choice: will: what the master wanted done
decisions.reason: The word means wish or intention.

decisions.choice: receive a heavy beating
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the number of blows, which the Greek leaves implied.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: ὁ δὲ μὴ γνοὺς ποιήσας δὲ ἄξια πληγῶν δαρήσεται ὀλίγας.
records.gloss: the [one] however not having known, having done however [things] worthy of stripes, will be beaten with few.
pieces: But a servant who did not know, though he did what deserved a beating, will get a lighter one.

L.48: but the one who did not know, and did things deserving of blows, will be beaten with few.

R.48: But a servant who does not know what his master wants, and does something that deserves punishment, will be whipped only a few times.

decisions.choice: beaten with few: those who did not know are still to blame, but less
alternatives: those who did not know go unpunished
decisions.reason: The law of Moses made a difference between sins done knowingly and those done in ignorance (Numbers 15:27-31). Not knowing lessens the blame but does not remove it.

decisions.choice: will get a lighter one
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the comparison with 12:47.

records.source: παντὶ δὲ ᾧ ἐδόθη πολύ, πολὺ ζητηθήσεται παρ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ᾧ παρέθεντο πολύ, περισσότερον αἰτήσουσιν αὐτόν.
records.gloss: Everyone now to whom was given much, much will be sought from him, and to whom was entrusted much, more abundantly they will ask him.
pieces: Much will be asked of everyone who has been given much. And when much has been put in someone's care, even more will be asked of {{gender:that person|him}}.

L.48: And from everyone to whom much was given, much will be required, and from the one to whom much was entrusted, they will ask all the more.

R.48: God expects much from people to whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given much. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has trusted someone with a great deal, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will ask even more from {{gender:that person|him}}.

decisions.choice: was given; was entrusted; they will ask: God gives, and God will ask
decisions.reason: The passives and the indefinite "they" point to God, as in 12:20.

decisions.choice: entrusted: given into someone's care to look after
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a deposit left in someone's keeping. What is entrusted must be accounted for.

decisions.choice: all the more: more than was given
decisions.reason: The word is a comparative. The second half of the saying goes further than the first.

decisions.choice: {{gender:that person|him}}
decisions.reason: The saying is for everyone; the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: God expects; he has given; he will ask
alternatives: much will be required; was given; they will ask
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: Πῦρ ἦλθον βαλεῖν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν, καὶ τί θέλω εἰ ἤδη ἀνήφθη;
records.gloss: Fire I came to cast upon the earth, and what I wish if already it were kindled!
pieces: I came to set fire to the earth, and how I long for it to be blazing already!

L.49: I came to cast fire upon the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!

R.49: I came to bring fire to the earth. I wish that it were already burning!

decisions.choice: fire: God's judgment, which also purifies, and which comes with the Holy Spirit
alternatives: the fire of the Spirit only
decisions.reason: John said that the one coming after him would baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire, and would burn up the chaff (3:16-17). Jesus' coming brings that fire: it tests and divides people (12:51-53).

decisions.choice: how I wish it were already kindled: a longing that is not yet fulfilled
alternatives: what do I want, if it is already kindled?
decisions.reason: The words can be read as a question, but they are best taken as a cry of longing, matching 12:50.

decisions.choice: bring
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain verb. Literal keeps "cast".

decisions.choice: set fire to
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the picture of lighting a fire, which 12:49b continues.

records.heading: Fire on the earth

records.source: βάπτισμα δὲ ἔχω βαπτισθῆναι, καὶ πῶς συνέχομαι ἕως ὅτου τελεσθῇ.
records.gloss: Baptism however I have to be baptized, and how I am distressed until that it be accomplished!
pieces: But first I must go through a baptism, and I am under great strain until it is over!

L.50: But I have a baptism to be baptized [with], and how I am pressed until it is completed!

R.50: But first I must suffer terrible things, as if a flood were going over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} head. I will be very troubled until it is finished!

decisions.choice: a baptism to be baptized with: his suffering and death
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the same picture in Mark 10:38-39. To be baptized is to be plunged under water, and in the Psalms deep waters picture overwhelming trouble (Psalm 42:8; 69:2-3).

decisions.choice: distressed: pressed hard, held in its grip
decisions.reason: The verb means to press together or hold fast. It can describe anguish (8:45; Philippians 1:23). Here Jesus is weighed down until his suffering is complete.

decisions.choice: accomplished: completed, brought to its end
decisions.reason: The verb is used of what Scripture says about Jesus being fulfilled (18:31; 22:37).

decisions.choice: first
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "first" to show that the baptism comes before the fire is lit (compare 17:25).

decisions.choice: suffer terrible things, as if a flood were going over my head
alternatives: a baptism to be baptized with
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture, as the meaning decision does.

decisions.choice: I am under great strain
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the verb in everyday words.

records.source: δοκεῖτε ὅτι εἰρήνην παρεγενόμην δοῦναι ἐν τῇ γῇ;
records.gloss: Do you think that peace I came to give on the earth?
pieces: Do you suppose that I came to bring peace to the earth?

L.51: Do you think that I came to give peace on the earth?

R.51: Do you think I came so that there would be peace in the world?

decisions.choice: peace: not peace with God, but an easy peace among people
decisions.reason: The angels announced peace on earth (2:14), and Jesus gives peace to those who trust him (7:50). But his coming also forces people to choose, and that divides them (2:34-35).

decisions.choice: world
decisions.reason: Readable says "world" for the earth as the home of people.

records.source: οὐχί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀλλ’ ἢ διαμερισμόν.
records.gloss: No, I say to you, but rather division.
pieces: No, I tell you, I came to bring division.

L.51: No, I tell you, but rather division.

R.51: No, I tell you. I came to make people take sides against each other.

decisions.choice: division: people split apart from one another
decisions.reason: Matthew 10:34 has "a sword"; Luke says what the sword does.

decisions.choice: I came to bring
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat the verb from 12:51a.

decisions.choice: make people take sides against each other
decisions.reason: Readable says what division means.

records.source: ἔσονται γὰρ ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν πέντε ἐν ἑνὶ οἴκῳ διαμεμερισμένοι, τρεῖς ἐπὶ δυσὶν καὶ δύο ἐπὶ τρισίν, διαμερισθήσονται πατὴρ ἐπὶ υἱῷ καὶ υἱὸς ἐπὶ πατρί, μήτηρ ἐπὶ θυγατέρα καὶ θυγάτηρ ἐπὶ τὴν μητέρα, πενθερὰ ἐπὶ τὴν νύμφην αὐτῆς καὶ νύμφη ἐπὶ τὴν πενθεράν.
records.gloss: There will be for from the now five in one house divided, three against two and two against three; \v 53 they will be divided father against son and son against father, mother against the daughter and daughter against the mother, mother-in-law against the daughter-in-law of her and daughter-in-law against the mother-in-law.
pieces: From now on, a family of five will be split, three against two and two against three.
Father will turn against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, a woman against her son's wife and the wife against her husband's mother."

L.52: For from now on there will be five in one household divided, three against two and two against three;
L.53: they will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law."

R.52: From now on, families will be divided. In a family of five people, three will be against two, and two will be against three.
R.53: Fathers and sons will be against each other. Mothers and daughters will be against each other. Mothers-in-law and daughters-in-law will be against each other."
