decisions.choice: father against son ... daughter-in-law against mother-in-law: Micah 7:6
decisions.reason: Micah described a time so evil that a man's enemies were the people of his own house. Jesus uses his words for the division that following him will bring into families.

decisions.choice: five in one house: a household of parents and a married son
decisions.reason: A son brought his wife to live in his parents' home. The five are father, mother, daughter, son, and son's wife: the people named in 12:53.

decisions.choice: from now on: from the time of Jesus' coming
alternatives: at the end of the world only
decisions.reason: The division has already begun (2:34-35).

decisions.choice: a woman against her son's wife and the wife against her husband's mother
decisions.reason: Balanced says who the in-laws are, which also shows the household of 12:52.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
decisions.reason: The narrator speaks again in 12:54.

records.source: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ τοῖς ὄχλοις· Ὅταν ἴδητε νεφέλην ἀνατέλλουσαν ἐπὶ δυσμῶν, εὐθέως λέγετε ὅτι Ὄμβρος ἔρχεται, καὶ γίνεται οὕτως·
records.gloss: He was saying now also to the crowds, When you see a cloud rising up from [the] west, immediately you say that, A rainstorm is coming, and it happens so;
pieces: Jesus also said to the crowds, "When you see a cloud coming up in the west, you say straight away, 'There will be rain,' and so there is.

L.54: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was also saying to the crowds, "When you see a cloud rising in the west, at once you say, 'A rainstorm is coming,' and so it happens.

R.54: Jesus also said to the crowds, "When you see clouds building up in the west, you say at once, 'Rain is on the way.' And you are right.

decisions.choice: a cloud in the west: rain coming in from the Mediterranean Sea
decisions.reason: In the land of Israel the sea lies to the west, and the rain clouds come from it (1 Kings 18:44).

decisions.choice: the crowds: the people as a whole, now addressed after the disciples
decisions.reason: Jesus turns from his disciples (12:22, 41) to the crowd (12:1).

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs on to 12:59; the people's sayings are in single quotation marks
decisions.reason: Jesus' words to the crowds in 12:54-59 are one speech.

records.heading: Reading the time

records.source: καὶ ὅταν νότον πνέοντα, λέγετε ὅτι Καύσων ἔσται, καὶ γίνεται.
records.gloss: and when a south wind is blowing, you say that, Heat will be, and it happens.
pieces: And when the south wind is blowing, you say, 'A scorching day is coming,' and so it turns out.

L.55: And when a south wind is blowing, you say, 'There will be scorching heat,' and it happens.

R.55: When the wind comes from the south, you say, 'It will be very hot today.' And it turns out hot.

decisions.choice: a south wind: hot, dry wind off the desert
decisions.reason: To the south and east of Israel lies desert. Wind from there brings burning heat (Job 37:17).

decisions.choice: scorching heat: burning heat
decisions.reason: The word is used of the heat of the sun (Matthew 20:12).

records.source: ὑποκριταί, τὸ πρόσωπον τῆς γῆς καὶ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ οἴδατε δοκιμάζειν, τὸν δὲ καιρὸν τοῦτον πῶς οὐκ οἴδατε δοκιμάζειν;
records.gloss: Hypocrites, the appearance of the earth and of the sky you know to discern, the however time this how not you know to discern?
pieces: You hypocrites! You can read the face of the earth and the sky. How is it, then, that you cannot read what this moment means?

L.56: Hypocrites! You know how to discern the face of the earth and of the sky, but how is it that you do not discern this time?

R.56: You are pretending! You can look at the earth and the sky and know what the weather will be. So why do you not understand what is happening now, at this time?

decisions.choice: hypocrites: people playing a part, here people who pretend they cannot see
alternatives: people who are insincere in everything
decisions.reason: The word is the one of 12:1. They read the weather well enough; their failure to read the time is not a lack of skill but an unwillingness to see.

decisions.choice: time: the moment God has set, the time of his coming in Jesus
decisions.reason: The word means a fitting or decisive time. Jesus' coming is God's time to visit his people (19:44).

decisions.choice: discern: test and judge, read the signs
decisions.reason: The verb is used of testing metals and so of judging what something is.

decisions.choice: You are pretending!
decisions.reason: Readable says what the word means here, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: read
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the everyday verb for reading the weather and the times.

records.source: Τί δὲ καὶ ἀφ’ ἑαυτῶν οὐ κρίνετε τὸ δίκαιον;
records.gloss: Why now even from yourselves not do you judge what [is] right?
pieces: Why can you not decide for yourselves what is right?

L.57: And why do you not, even on your own, judge what is right?

R.57: You should be able to decide for yourselves what is right to do.

decisions.choice: right: just, what ought to be done
decisions.reason: The word is the adjective "righteous", here meaning what is just and fitting in this situation. The next verses show what is right: to settle with one's opponent before it is too late.

decisions.choice: even for yourselves: without waiting to be told
decisions.reason: They should see what the time calls for without needing signs from others (11:29).

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: Readable gives the point of the question.

records.source: ὡς γὰρ ὑπάγεις μετὰ τοῦ ἀντιδίκου σου ἐπ’ ἄρχοντα, ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ δὸς ἐργασίαν ἀπηλλάχθαι ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ, μήποτε κατασύρῃ σε πρὸς τὸν κριτήν, καὶ ὁ κριτής σε παραδώσει τῷ πράκτορι, καὶ ὁ πράκτωρ σε βαλεῖ εἰς φυλακήν.
records.gloss: As for you are going with the adversary of you before a ruler, on the way give effort to be released from him, lest he drag you to the judge, and the judge you will hand over to the officer, and the officer you will throw into prison.
pieces: When someone is taking you to court before the magistrate, do your best to settle with {{gender:them|him}} while you are still on the way. If you do not, your accuser may drag you before the judge. The judge may hand you over to the officer, and the officer may throw you into prison.

L.58: For as you are going with your opponent before a magistrate, make an effort on the way to be set free from {{gender:them|him}}, so that {{gender:they|he}} do not drag you to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.

R.58: Suppose someone is taking you to court. While you are on the way there, do all you can to settle the matter with that person. If you do not, that person may drag you in front of the judge. The judge may give you to the officer, and the officer will put you in prison.

decisions.choice: opponent: someone suing you, probably over a debt; officer: the court official who collected debts
decisions.reason: The word for the opponent is a legal one. The officer was the one who carried out the court's ruling and could hold a debtor in prison until the debt was paid (12:59; Matthew 5:25-26).

decisions.choice: settle on the way: a picture of the need to make peace with God before the judgment
decisions.reason: After 12:54-57 the saying is more than advice about courts. Those who read the time should put things right with God while there is still time.

decisions.choice: make an effort to be set free from him: try hard to settle the case
decisions.reason: The phrase means to work at being released from the claim, by coming to terms with the accuser.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: The opponent may be a man or a woman; the inclusive form is the default, as in Matthew 5:25.

decisions.choice: settle the matter with that person
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom.

decisions.choice: the situation first, then the advice
alternatives: As you are going with your opponent ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable set out the case before saying what to do, as Matthew 5:25 does.

records.source: λέγω σοι, οὐ μὴ ἐξέλθῃς ἐκεῖθεν ἕως καὶ τὸ ἔσχατον λεπτὸν ἀποδῷς.
records.gloss: I say to you, not not you will come out from there until even the last lepton you have paid.
pieces: I tell you, there will be no way out for you until {{units:the very last penny|the very last lepton}} is paid."

L.59: I tell you, you will never get out of there until you have paid even the last lepton."

R.59: I tell you, you will not get out of prison until you have paid {{units:every last cent|every last lepton}}."

decisions.choice: lepton: the smallest coin in use
decisions.reason: A lepton was a tiny copper coin worth half a quadrans (Mark 12:42), a hundred and twenty-eighth of a denarius, the day's wage of a laborer. The widow put two of them into the temple treasury (21:2). The debt must be paid to the last coin.

decisions.choice: never: a strong double negative
decisions.reason: The Greek uses two negatives together for an emphatic denial.

decisions.choice: {{units:the very last penny|the very last lepton}} (B); {{units:every last cent|every last lepton}} (R)
alternatives: the last lepton at every level
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the modern smallest coin by default, with the original coin as the alternative, as Matthew 5:26 does. Literal keeps the original coin.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
decisions.reason: The speech that began in 12:54 ends with the chapter.
